applicability: Only channels.json entries, not arbitrary visually adjacent triples.
logic: State the anchor/entry theme, then the supporting or balancing theme, then the channel-specific midpoint. All nodes retain their role. Avoid repeating a whole archetype profile.
example: A 3 entry suggests examining tangible care and resources; a 21 midpoint adds broad or cross-context work settings; an 18 bridge calls for clarifying assumptions between partnership and money.
exceptions: This is original report composition. It does not certify a named traditional program.

applicability: The nine primary nodes only: day, month, year, bottom, core, nw, ne, se, sw.
logic: Group equal values across distinct nodes. Mention at most two recurring themes, with every contributing node listed. Interpret as structural recurrence; dependent sums are not independent evidence. Do not count channels, report occurrences, family_center or purposes as more primary observations.
example: The same 5 appears at bottom and ne. Learning appears both as a personal challenge theme and a maternal upper-branch theme. This does not show that your mother had that trait.
exceptions: No power score, multiplier, probability or diagnosis.

applicability: Only the listed pairs in contrast_pairs.json and only within one section's declared nodes.
logic: Present two useful preferences and a tradeoff; offer a conditional behavior example and a practical agreement. Never decide that one cancels the other. Use at most one contrast per section.
example: Structure (4) and exploration (22) can be negotiated through stable commitments and a bounded experiment.
exceptions: No conflict score and no claim that a person actually experiences the tradeoff.

logic: Explain the bridge once as the place where resource and relationship commitments meet; link back to it in both sections.
example: If uncertainty is the bridge theme, distinguish the shared facts about time and money from expectations each person assumed.
exceptions: No wealth forecast or meeting-place prediction.

logic: Look up karmic_patterns.json by the three named roles in calculation order. If absent, use the bottom archetype as a general learning theme and explicitly state that no named pattern was matched.
example: For 1991-12-09, 5-15-20 matches TAIL-C-5-15-20. Physical order 5-20-15 is different and is not a lookup key.
exceptions: No sorting, reversing, or multiset matching. No literal accusation about a past life.

logic: Offer one practical work experiment joining a talent-related practice with the resource midpoint theme; display both underlying roles.
example: Expression through service (12) with a broad coordination theme (21) could be explored by making one useful guide for a specific new audience.
exceptions: An exploration, not an assurance of income or professional fit.
